stewardship.deescalation: Not applicable to antibiotics. Once species is confirmed, ensure species-appropriate antimalarial therapy is given (e.g., artemisinin-based combination therapy for P. falciparum per national guidelines; chloroquine plus primaquine for P. vivax in chloroquine-sensitive regions, with G6PD testing before primaquine).
framework: This is a parasitic, not bacterial, infection — antibiotics provide no benefit and should not be given for malaria itself.
Confirm species by peripheral smear (gold standard, also allows parasite density quantification) or rapid diagnostic test before starting species-specific antimalarial therapy.

Watch closely for severity criteria (P. falciparum): impaired consciousness, acidosis, hypoglycemia, severe anemia, renal impairment, pulmonary edema, significant bleeding, shock, or high parasitemia — any of these mandate IV artesunate and higher level of care, not oral therapy.

references: National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme (NVBDCP) India Guidelines
